Harry Halliday was an English cricketer born on April 22, 1855, in Westhoughton, Lancashire. He was a right-handed batsman and a right-arm medium-fast bowler. Halliday's cricket career was primarily in the late 19th century, and he played first-class cricket between 1876 and 1888.

Halliday played for several teams, including Lancashire and a number of other regional teams. He is noted for his contributions to the game during a period when cricket was evolving, especially in terms of techniques and playing styles.

Throughout his career, Halliday often demonstrated solid performances, although he may not be as widely remembered as some of his contemporaries. His playing style and statistics would reflect the state of the game during his time.

Harry Halliday passed away on January 24, 1935. His contributions to cricket, particularly through the clubs and regions he represented, remain a part of the rich history of the sport in England.
